spec_match.rationale: Every request on these pages is a real PaymentRequest for the secure-payment-confirmation method with a complete data object, and the central claim — that the locale is checked at the dialog rather than at construction — is measured rather than quoted: ['zz'] and [] both construct. The locale-matching demonstration uses Intl, and says explicitly that it answers a related question with the same data rather than the dialog's own.

interactive.rationale: A live request builder with six deliberate quirks, each constructed for real; a locale-list evaluator that canonicalises, checks data availability and resolves a best-fit match against the user's own languages; and a checkout pre-flight that runs five real checks and picks a payment path from the result.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index frames the change as a mixed-language dialog problem — the browser's words around the merchant's — which is the specification's own reasoning, and states up front that these pages stop before show().

edge_cases.rationale: An empty locale list, a well-formed but unreal tag, a malformed tag that Intl throws on, an empty credentialIds list, a circular reference, and the getter pair. It also covers the case where the failure is NOT a locale problem — no credential — and says the checkout should not treat it as one.

references.rationale: chromestatus.com/feature/5126146013396992 on the index and all three concept pages, with the SPC locale field, the Payment Request API and MDN's Intl.getCanonicalLocales.

conformance.rationale: Seven immutable assertions: PaymentRequest exists; an SPC request constructs; a nonsense and an empty locale both construct (the framing the demos depend on); method data is JSON-serialised so a throwing getter is a TypeError while a value-returning one is fine; canMakePayment answers without a gesture, which is what makes a pre-flight possible; Intl can canonicalise, query and resolve; and navigator.languages is readable.

runtime_evidence.rationale: deno task drive over all three pages in real Chrome 150: 3/3, 31 assertions. Verified: requests construct with every locale value including ['zz'] and []; a throwing getter fails with a JSON-serialisation TypeError while a value-returning getter constructs fine; canMakePayment() resolves false on this machine; tag canonicalisation, data availability and best-fit resolution all behave; and the pre-flight completes six steps and chooses a path. NOT verified: the NotSupportedError itself. It arrives from show(), which needs a user gesture and an enrolled credential — this machine has neither, and the pages say so where a reader will see it.

telemetry_health.rationale: Each page emits showcaseTelemetry.assert with the constructed state, the locale list, the resolution, and the pre-flight's failures and chosen path.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, no raw colour literals, buttons set background and colour, 44px control minimums, and the wide tables in their own scroll containers.

accessibility.rationale: Every control is labelled; the pre-flight steps state their outcome in words before their reason; tables carry row headers and updating captions; results are announced through aria-live; the payload block is focusable so it can be scrolled from the keyboard.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Control grids are auto-fit minmax and stack at 360px; the payload and every table scroll inside their own containers; the checkout block is a simple flex column. Payments are disproportionately a mobile flow, and nothing here assumes a pointer.

openQuestions.title: The refusal itself has never been seen
openQuestions.detail: Everything on these pages leads up to a NotSupportedError that no run has produced, because show() needs a gesture and a credential. Enrolling a test credential against a local relying party and driving show() by hand would produce the error these pages are about — and would settle whether the message names the locale or is as unhelpful as the serialisation one. That is the single most valuable follow-up.

openQuestions.title: Intl's locale data is a proxy, not the dialog's translation set
openQuestions.detail: The matching page uses Intl.DateTimeFormat.supportedLocalesOf as a stand-in for whether Chrome has a payment dialog in a language, and labels it as necessary-not-sufficient. The real set is smaller and is not exposed to script. If it ever becomes observable, the page should use it; until then the caveat is doing real work and should not be quietly dropped.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible form controls driving a live preview
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Label every control, recompute on input rather than behind a submit, and keep the relationship between a control and what it changes obvious.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: All three pages rebuild on input: the request is reconstructed on every keystroke, the tag table re-evaluates as you type, and the checkout total follows the amount. The one thing behind a button is the pre-flight, because it makes an asynchronous call.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: deno task drive changes selects and inputs and asserts the recomputed output on each page.

guidanceConsulted.query: announce a multi step check result in a live region
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: State each step's outcome in words, not only by colour, and summarise in a live region when the sequence finishes.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Each pre-flight step prints 'ok' or 'no' as text before its explanation, and the summary names which preconditions failed. The skipped final step says why it was skipped rather than being omitted.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: deno task drive asserts the sixth step is present, marked skipped, and explains that it only happens at show().

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive control panel and wide table without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: auto-fit grids for controls; wide tables and code blocks in their own scroll containers.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied throughout; the payload block is additionally height-capped with its own vertical scroll so a long request does not push the rest of the page away.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: responsive-check desktop + mobile on the feature.

summary: Three concepts about an error that cannot be produced here, built around everything that can. The build corrected itself twice: a getter that returns a value does NOT break the request (only one that throws does), and rendering the payload of a throwing-getter request runs the same getter — so this page hit exactly the failure it was documenting, which is now what the page says.
